stories.headline: KMT Chairwoman Cheng Li-wun meets Xi Jinping in Beijing, China announces 10 Taiwan measures
stories.summary: Taiwan's main opposition KMT leader Cheng Li-wun conducted a controversial 'peace mission' to China, meeting with Xi Jinping on April 10. Following the meeting, China announced 10 new policy measures targeting Taiwan, including resuming flights and establishing regular KMT-CCP communication channels.

stories.headline: President Lai Ching-te meets multiple US congressional delegations
stories.summary: President Lai held several meetings with US officials including a bipartisan Senate Foreign Relations Committee delegation led by Jeanne Shaheen, a Republican Study Committee delegation, and Senator Jim Banks. The meetings reaffirmed US-Taiwan security ties and discussed defense cooperation.

stories.headline: President Lai inaugurates National Center for AI Robotics, promotes Taiwan's tech development
stories.summary: President Lai officially opened the National Center for AI Robotics in Tainan on April 10, calling it crucial for Taiwan's goal of becoming a technology-oriented island. The center is part of the government's Ten AI Infrastructure Projects aimed at strengthening Taiwan's competitive edge in AI development.

stories.headline: Taiwan detects increased Chinese military activity around the island
stories.summary: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense reported detecting multiple Chinese aircraft sorties and naval vessels operating around Taiwan on several dates, with many aircraft crossing the median line and entering Taiwan's Air Defense Identification Zone. Activities included 17 aircraft and 7 vessels detected on one day.

stories.headline: TSMC reports record Q1 revenue driven by AI chip demand
stories.summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company reported first-quarter revenue of NT$1.13 trillion ($35.6 billion), a 35% year-on-year increase, beating market forecasts. The strong performance was driven by sustained demand for AI chips from customers like Apple and Nvidia.

stories.headline: Taiwan People's Party expels legislator Li Zhenxiu
stories.summary: The Taiwan People's Party expelled at-large legislator Li Zhenxiu following controversies, effectively stripping her of her legislative seat. The expulsion came after she made disputed claims during a livestream and was referred to the party's disciplinary committee.

stories.headline: President Lai warns against compromising with authoritarian regimes
stories.summary: President Lai stated that peace cannot be achieved by compromising with authoritarian regimes, warning this would undermine Taiwan's sovereignty and democracy. He made these comments while pushing for approval of a supplementary defense budget amid China's gray-zone activities.

stories.headline: Ex-TV producer indicted for spying for China
stories.summary: Taiwan's Taipei District Prosecutors Office indicted former television producer Lee Neng-chien for allegedly collecting Taiwanese military intelligence for China, seeking a prison sentence of at least 12 years. He allegedly obtained over 3,000 pieces of personal data including military personnel information.

articles.title: Ex-TV producer indicted for spying for China, faces 12-year sentence
